subject: Re: Deployment mode & data residency follow-up (EU/APAC) - next steps
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Schmidt <oliver.schmidt@finserv-eu.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:15:00 -0400
Subject: Follow-up: deployment mode & data residency (EU/APAC)

Hi Oliver —

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align with procurement and your security team: 

What we heard:
- Primary requirement: EU-only data residency for production PII workloads.
- Secondary: potential APAC users later this year; discuss cross-region routing and replication.
- Preference to avoid traffic leaving EU for inference or KV storage.

Options we discussed (high level):
1) Hosted API (EU region): fastest to ship, hosted in EU cloud region. Good if EU-only routing is strictly enforced and EU region meets your control requirements. We can enable EU-only model hosting and KMS in-region.
2) Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools in an EU region (SLA-backed), gives stronger isolation and predictable throughput with single-tenant pools. Still hosted by Redwood but isolated to your account.
3) Private (VPC or on-prem): full customer-managed VPC or on-prem package for strict compliance / audit needs. Best for customers who require control-plane separation or air-gapped operation.

Questions for your team (helps us size and recommend):
- Which deployment mode are you leaning toward (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)?
- Target monthly prompt+completion tokens (est.) and peak QPS/latency SLOs.
- Are any regulatory controls required beyond EU-only residency (e.g., in-region KMS, no cross-region backups)?
- Timeline for procurement and pilot (we can prepare a Dedicated capacity PO or Private deployment proposal).

I attached a short one-pager comparing the three options and the data-residency checklist. Happy to jump on a quick follow-up with Aditya (technical) and Marissa (security/compliance) to answer detailed questions.

Best,
Lauren
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: redwood-deployment-options-one-pager.pdf (1 page)
Attachment: finserv-data-residency-checklist.xlsx (excel)

From: Oliver Schmidt <oliver.schmidt@finserv-eu.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finserv-eu.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 13:02:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment mode & data residency (EU/APAC)

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the clear recap. Helpful. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Residency: production data must remain in EU at all times. We cannot have inference or KV cache leave the EU.
- KMS: keys must be customer-managed (bring-your-own-key) and hosted in an EU KMS.
- Pilot: we'd like to run a 3-week pilot with ~500k tokens/day to validate latency and cost.
- Timeline: procurement and legal are targeting a June PO window.

Initial leaning: Dedicated capacity if Redwood can guarantee EU-only routing and in-region KMS. Private VPC is our fallback if the above cannot be guaranteed or if legal asks for additional control-plane separation.

Can Aditya share a few details on how Dedicated enforces EU-only routing (no fallback to other regions) and how KMS integration would look? Also please share the cost ballpark for a Dedicated monthly commit vs Private deployment baseline for the pilot.

Oliver
Oliver Schmidt | Head of AI Platforms, FinServ EU
oliver.schmidt@finserv-eu.com
+49 30 1234 5678

From: aditya.rao@redwood.com <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Oliver Schmidt <oliver.schmidt@finserv-eu.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 13:48:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment mode & data residency (EU/APAC)

Hi Oliver —

Quick technical notes on Dedicated + EU-only routing and KMS integration: 

- Dedicated pools: we can provision a dedicated GPU pool in an EU region (we've done this for several banking customers). All inference nodes, KV caches, and persistent stores for that pool live in-region.
- Network controls: traffic is routed via regional load balancers; we can enforce ingress/egress ACLs and block inter-region fallback at the routing layer. We will include this in the SLA.
- KMS: Redwood supports customer-managed keys (BYOK) via AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, or HashiCorp Vault in customer VPCs. For Dedicated we can integrate your EU KMS and ensure keys never leave region. For Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) keys live under your control.
- Cross-region replication: we disable replication by default; if you later want APAC read-replicas for lower latency to APAC users, that is opt-in and will require additional controls/consent.

I'll prepare a short technical appendix showing network flow and KMS integration patterns. Happy to join a call with your security/infra folks.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com

Thanks for the quick replies. Next steps I suggest:

Thanks,
Lauren
